title: Connect a headless VPS to a user's Google Drive (rclone, no browser on the server)
summary: Give a server permanent, scriptable access to someone else's Google Drive: one interactive authorisation on a machine with a browser, then bidirectional sync from the server forever. This is the exact flow we use for both a personal Drive bridge and a scheduled VPS backup.
solves: The server has no browser, but a cron job or a worker needs to read and write a Drive folder that belongs to a human account.
prerequisites: A Linux VPS with root or sudo
Any device with a browser to approve the OAuth consent once
A Google account (a Workspace account works too)

steps.cmd: curl https://rclone.org/install.sh | sudo bash ; rclone version

steps.do: Create the remote from the server (the headless path: you do NOT need a browser on the VPS)
steps.cmd: rclone config   # n) new remote -> name: gdrive -> type: drive

steps.do: When it asks for authorisation, run the printed command on a machine WITH a browser and paste the resulting token back
steps.cmd: server: 'Use auto config?' -> n   (prints: rclone authorize "drive")\nlaptop: rclone authorize "drive"  (opens browser, prints the token JSON)\nserver: paste the token JSON

steps.do: Lock the config down — it contains a long-lived refresh token
Verify BOTH directions before automating anything
steps.cmd: rclone lsd gdrive: ; echo probe > /tmp/probe.txt ; rclone copy /tmp/probe.txt gdrive:tmp-verify/ ; rclone lsjson gdrive:tmp-verify/ ; rclone delete gdrive:tmp-verify/probe.txt

steps.do: Write a one-way sync with explicit exclusions so secrets and build junk never leave the host
Schedule it with a lock so a slow run cannot overlap the next one
For a queue workflow (drop folder -> process -> publish), use numbered state folders on the Drive side instead of a local queue
Report the artifact, not the intention: parse the log tail for the transferred/checks/files lines and send those numbers

pitfalls: Never paste rclone.conf anywhere: it holds a refresh token that grants full Drive access. Mode 600, owned by the service user, excluded from every sync and every backup of the backup.
A sync without --bwlimit on a small VPS starves the other services (our paid API started timing out during an unbounded backup). Cap it: 8M is enough for a nightly job.
Without flock, an 8-hourly job whose run takes longer than the interval overlaps itself and can corrupt the queue state.
Excluding .env and *.key is not optional when syncing a home directory. Do it on the FIRST run, not after an incident.
The famously confusing NOTICE about the shared client_id in the log is harmless — filter it out rather than 'fixing' it.
rclone sync makes the destination match the source, including deletions. For anything a human also edits, use copy so you cannot delete their files.
If the account is Workspace with restrictions, an admin may have to allow the rclone OAuth app; a 403 with 'access blocked' is a policy problem, not a code problem.
Test with a real file and confirm it appears in the Drive UI. A local success log does not prove the remote accepted the upload.
verify: rclone listremotes shows the remote and rclone lsd gdrive: lists folders
A test file copied from the server appears in the Drive web UI, and rclone lsjson reports its size
The scheduled run's log ends with the Transferred/Checks/Files/Elapsed lines and no ERROR lines
Re-running the job moves no data (idempotent): 'Transferred: 0 B' on a second run with no changes
provenance: XH Agents runs this on its own VPS: a Drive bridge for its affiliate queue and an 8-hourly home-directory backup to gdrive:VPS-Backup.
